requirements.requirement: Repair bin/replay so pending messages are delivered exactly once per Message-ID while retaining distinct messages that share a subject.
requirements.summary: The repaired replay delivered one copy of <a@branch.test>, skipped its duplicate, and separately delivered <b@branch.test>; both retained Subject: Notice. The final index has exactly one entry for each Message-ID, including after restart.

requirements.requirement: Re-running recovery must skip messages already recorded in delivered/index.tsv.
requirements.summary: A bounded rerun skipped all valid indexed spool entries, produced identical before/after hashes, added no files, and retained one index entry per Message-ID. The post-restart rerun behaved identically.

requirements.requirement: Preserve the original spool and the already-delivered message.
requirements.summary: Final evidence shows all four original spool files still present with hashes matching the prepared baseline, while delivered/old.eml retained its original content hash. These remained intact after restart.

requirements.requirement: Place malformed messages in quarantine with an explanation.
requirements.summary: The malformed bad.eml was copied unchanged into quarantine with a companion reason containing “missing Message-ID header”; both persisted through reruns and restart.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Ubuntu 7.10 and kernel 2.6.22-14-generic were directly observed before and after the work and after restart. The POSIX-shell replay executed successfully using installed legacy utilities.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. Replay now deduplicates by Message-ID, preserves same-subject distinct messages and original data, quarantines malformed mail with a reason, and is idempotent. The legacy OS and kernel were retained. The mandatory node-restart evidence protocol was also fully demonstrated and independently corroborated. Hygiene is reduced modestly for a reverted, scoped troubleshooting attempt that temporarily misclassified valid mail.
limitations: Failed-service inspection was unsupported because this legacy image lacks systemctl; no service-specific functionality was required by the task, and the remaining lifecycle checks showed no package, socket, or temporary-file regression.
Requirement R3 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: Final hygiene is good: no executor-caused temporary-file residue, new listening sockets, or package damage was observed. The required restart protocol was complete, with healthy pre-restart state, acknowledgement, a changed boot identity independently corroborated by lifecycle observations, and full recovered task state. Three bounded unnecessary mutations occurred during troubleshooting: cmd-16e9abb426a64407 installed a flawed replay implementation that was later replaced; cmd-28a190b305844557 ran it and temporarily created false quarantine copies and reasons for three valid messages; and cmd-661bc6f4900c42ae applied an interim parser edit later superseded by the final rewrite. The false quarantine artifacts were removed by cmd-661bc6f4900c42ae, and the flawed/interim script versions were replaced by cmd-5e8ec95dafad42af, so none of this residue remained. The cleanup portion of cmd-661bc6f4900c42ae was corrective and is not itself penalized.
